utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Registrar. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case Number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, Mr. Oric, the usual question. I want to make sure that you are following the proceedings in a language that you can understand.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour, gentlemen. Yes, I can follow the proceedings in a language I can understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you and you may sit down. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Jan Wubben, senior trial attorney, together with counsel, Ms. Patricia Sellers, Ms. Joanne Richardson, and our case manager, Ms. Donnica Henry-Frijlink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and good morning to your team. Appearances for Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. I am Vasvija Vidovic together with Mr. John Jones, representing Mr. Naser Oric. And we have our legal assistant with us, Ms. Jasmina Cosic, and our CaseMap manager Mr. Geoff Roberts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Vidovic, and good morning to you and the rest of your team. Do you have any preliminaries on your part? We have got some. Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: We hand over the confidential witness list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Without mentioning any names, I would like to refer to it. It is of course tentative as there is a motion pending regarding the videolink. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but the persons mentioned for the purpose of the videolink are included here, no?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. What I would require from you, Madam Vidovic, is these are two hours, three hours is the estimate of what you need for yourselves, no?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So then we would require you, Madam Vidovic, to more or less give us an indication of how much you require.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we would need approximately the same time required by the Prosecution for our cross-examination. But this time, when we are speaking about Ms. Racine Manas, perhaps we would need an hour and a half for that. And of course about Dr. Gow, we already said that I hope that we would manage to complete his cross-examination in two days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Where does Mr. Gow have to come from?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, he's in London. He's not far away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. So if we find ourselves in a fix and we have to move by one day, two days, his testimony, that's not going to affect -- if we tell you beforehand, obviously.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: As long as we are given some warning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. But I suggest that you -- the 29th is Monday, no? The 29th is a Monday. So I would advise Mr. Gow to allow for the entire week if necessary, because if we say -- we don't start on Monday with him, we start on Tuesday, if we don't start on Tuesday, we start on Wednesday, we want to be sure that he is available from the beginning to the end of his testimony, which I understand would take us anything from two and a half to three days.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I will advise Mr. Gow to try to set aside that amount of time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That week. And as we approach the date, we should be in a better position to give -- to put you in a position to advise him accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thanks. So any preliminaries on your part? Two things. We are still waiting for your response to the Defence motion for adjudicated facts.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That's in preparation. I believe the Prosecution will file that today, at the latest tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. That's number one. The other one is we are still waiting for your response to the Prosecution motion for protective measures, the one that was filed ten days ago on the 18th.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, Your Honour and we will be filing a response today or tomorrow. And that also applied to the videolink motion of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. We are not making an order. We are just indicating our strong desire that you comply with this and that you file it by not later than tomorrow. Wednesday I leave, so -- I have discussed all these matters with Judges Brydensholt and Eser already. We are going to do our utmost to have these matters decided by Tuesday, but we can't neither discuss nor decide unless we have got the responses from either side.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, we can assure you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That will help us immensely if you file everything by the end of the business day tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, might I add we are willing to provide courtesy copies so you might be able to have that before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. There being no other business to transact, I suggest that Madam Usher brings in the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, upon arrival of the witness, if I may ask for private session due to a request for protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But can his face be seen or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: The face will be part of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's go into private session immediately before we mess it up. Let's go into private session for the time being because we are in Trial Chamber II you are going to tell me. I don't know whether there are transmissions, so let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session now. Just for the record, the Trial Chamber has been in private session to consider and decide upon an oral submission made by the witness for the granting of a protective measure consisting in facial distortion, which the Trial Chamber has granted after hearing the parties and the witness herself. Now, you are going to give evidence. The way we go about it here is that first a senior officer from the Prosecution will ask you a number of questions, which you need to answer fully and truthfully. Then, one of the lawyers defending the accused will ask you another series of questions on cross-examination. And even then you are required by law to answer truthfully and fully. Did I make myself clear? Madam, did you hear what I said? Was it translated to you? Are you receiving interpretation in your own language? Please answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you understand what I explained to you before, namely what's going to happen, that you are going to be asked questions by both sides and that you are bound to answer all questions truthfully and fully?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know what I've already said yesterday. I don't know about this now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but we were not there yesterday. There was only Mr. Wubben, I would imagine, yesterday. So we need to hear the story now, and it's only you who can tell us the story and not Mr. Wubben. So, Mr. Wubben, I give you the floor. Could you please start with your direct and regards the basics, you can lead the witness. If -- because otherwise it won't make sense. If we need to go into private session for a short while, for a short while, so that we get the details, personal details, from the witness, I think we could do that because otherwise it's a question of facial distortion doesn't really make sense. Shall we go into private session for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session for a while before the witness tells us exactly who she is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session. Please proceed, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Mrs. Djokic, can you tell the Judges what happened in the past when it comes to the village you lived in.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It happened in our village on the 5th of October. There was a man chopping wood near my house and my son had gone to Bajina Basta to do some shopping for the family patron saint's day, St. Michael. I was at home washing the linen and getting ready for this religious feast. Once my son was back from Bajina Basta, he came to me and said, Mom is there anything to eat? I said, Yes, there is, call your father and brother -- husband, and wait for me right there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Wubben, we need to establish the name of the village, please. And unless we are going to be put in a position where we are going to have to intervene --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The village of Divovici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Try to direct the witness to answer the question and nothing but the question because otherwise we are going to have long stories.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I intended to do so. It was an opening question also enabling the witness to do the first opening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So you lived then in the village of Divovici. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Is it a hamlet or a village and are there other hamlets around?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there are hamlets, Kutijese, Boljevici, Radijevici, Divovici. And then behind, Zanjevo. There is Zanjevo. Behind Zanjevo there is Fakovici down there, further down.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: How many kilometres from Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, that's difficult to say, I'm illiterate. I don't know how many kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Those hamlets or villages around your hamlet where you lived, were these all Serb hamlets or other ethnic origin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Serb hamlets. Kutijese, Boljevici, Radijevici, Divovici. And after Divovici there is Zanjevo which was a Muslim hamlet. And then behind this Muslim hamlet there was Fakovici. And then Grabovica. And then further down, towards the Drina, there were other hamlets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session for one question I would like to put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed, Mr. Wubben. And my apologies for interrupting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I will proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: You mentioned this hamlet or village of Zanjevo. It is a Muslim village. Did you have any problems with that hamlet at that time or the inhabitants of your village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before the war we had no problems at all, no problems at all. We lived side by side. We worked together. Whatever was necessary. It couldn't have been better. During this catastrophe, this war, whoever tore us apart, I have no idea. Before the war everything was fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many houses, farmhouses or homes, there were in your village or hamlet called Divovici at that time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Divovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Seven, eight, nine, ten houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And in the hamlet of --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 11, 11 houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And in the other hamlet of Radijevici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Radijevici, I can't say, there are some.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: When the tension started during the war, was there a kind of guard or military or none at all, as far as you can confirm, in your village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. There was a little guard that night. There were people there. They were working. Nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Were these guards, were they soldiers or not? Civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And did they wear uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Did they have uniforms, apart from the fact that they didn't wear it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So these village guards consisted of civilians, but was there any military presence in the village, any equipment, soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, nothing. No military. If there had been any military there present, this would not have been allowed to happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: You mentioned something happened on the 5th of October. Was that in the year of the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What happened. On the 5th of October, then there was nothing much. And then there was a strike, an attack down the Drina River valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: My question is to the witness: How long ago was that, that 5th of October, how many years?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think 11 or 12 years since.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And what happened on the 5th of October?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told you what happened. My son left for Bajina Basta to do some shopping for the family patron saint's holiday. My husband was chopping wood and my son-in-law was brewing brandy. I was washing our Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond linen at a well. My son came back from Bajina Basta and said was there anything to eat. Then they went there. And then there was an explosion up there. We were at the barn and then I went back to the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Witness, will you please stop. Thank you for the answer, but I will ask some questions and then please give an answer focussed to that question. My next question is: On that particular day, the 5th of October, you said it is around 11 or 12 years ago. Was it 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I am illiterate. I can't even pronounce it. Or who. I know that the 12th, or rather it was the 5th of October. What the date was or the year, I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: You were working together with others or you stayed at the farm at that particular day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Did you have any animals in that farm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, goats, a cow, some swine.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: You were in that farm on that particular with your son and your husband?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And also others, or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My stepson was there. He was brewing brandy and the rest had gone to the field to pick the corn.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And what happened then? Can you please describe that to the Judges.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When that happened, Pero stormed into the house when the attack occurred. He ran into the house. He took his rifle that he kept in the house. My son came into the room and he took the rifle and went from the room to the kitchen and -- from the room to the kitchen and from the kitchen to the hall. We couldn't go any further because by then we were surrounded and we couldn't go anywhere. We stayed right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes. How did you know that there was a kind of attack? Can you tell us what you heard or saw.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We heard sounds of shooting. We heard an explosion in the house and the shooting began.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Who was --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We stayed in the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges who was shooting.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Who was shooting? Muslims, or least that's what my son told me. He said, Mom, this is Nasir Orlic [Realtime transcript read in error: Oric"]. It must be he and his army.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So you heard from your --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's an error in the transcript. The witness said Nasir Orlic and it's come out as Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I have no teeth. I may have mispronounced it. I can't get everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but what is the name you wanted to give us? What was this man's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nasir Orlic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's what she said.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So this is what your son said to you. But did you by yourself look out the window or the door of your house and saw men or whoever outside if so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My son was at the window and at the door. He didn't allow me to go and have a look. Because he said if I had gone myself I would have gotten very scared. So he wouldn't let me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And did you hear in the meanwhile that shooting from outside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, from outside, yes. We did. Outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And what did you and your son subsequently do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We stayed in the house. We defended ourselves. He showed me how to put the cartridge into the rifle. We had to defend ourselves. We had nowhere to go from the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So your son was someone as a kind of village guard, or is that a wrong conclusion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was there as a guard. He didn't go any further. At home, that's where he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And your husband, was he a member of the village guard as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, right there. The army, the village, the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And your son had a gun. And your husband at that very time, did he also wear a gun with him or an arm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No. On the 5th of October he didn't. He was chopping wood. And none of them had any weapons on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And did your husband wear a uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And did your son wear a uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So your son had a gone or something like that. Did you notice what it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know what kind it was. I don't know. I don't know what it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And please describe what happened then.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then we, he and we defended ourselves from the house. And then when he took my cow away, Svetozar told me he took my cow away and the goat and he chased them away. He took the door down and put it into a basket.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Svetozar told you. Svetozar is your son? Can you confirm that Svetozar is the name of your son.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now, had there been any contact between you or your son and that army outside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No. None whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Did you yell at them or they yelled at you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We didn't yell at them and they were yelling --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: What were they yelling --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- at us. They said, Come out, come out, you bloody Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: What did you make out of that, this kind of language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes. Did you yell back? Did someone show up or whatsoever?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We didn't respond at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So you stayed in the house with your son. And what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't get the answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We stayed in the house. And then we were there. And then we defended ourselves from the house. Then Stojka came along. Stojka came to us and she was yelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Who is Stojka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Stojka is Marko's. She came to us and she was yelling, Savka, come on. My sister, come out. They are all our neighbours. They will not harm us. There, you can see my children outside naked down to the waist. And then she left and she came back. And she said, Svetozar, my beautiful son, come out. These people are all our neighbours and no harm will come to us. And you can see my children out there, they are naked to the waist and then she came in.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So this woman came into your house, but before she came into your house she was with those men outside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With those people there, the enemies. How should I put it? The army they had over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And this Stojka was -- had Serbian ethnic origin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And the others outside, the same origin, Serbian, or another origin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw no Serbs. When I was in the house -- while I was in the house, the Serbs had gone to the fields to do their work there. We stayed home, and my nephew was brewing brandy and I was doing some Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond washing and he was chopping wood and my son came.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: After Stojka left your house when she came in, she left the house, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And then she came again and she said -- she grabbed Svetozar -- she grabbed his rifle in the hall and Svetozar said, Leave my rifle alone or I'll kill you right here at the doorstep. So she let his rifle go. She left and came back. And they told her to go and set my house alight. And she said, Listen, children, why should I set any houses on fire? So she came and she didn't set fire to our house. And Svetozar then threw her out. And she was in the hall and she didn't leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: We'll get back later on this gun she took. But first let me ask you in the meanwhile when this all happened, what happened to your husband, if so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was killed in front of the shed, at home. And Svetozar told me, Mom, look. Dad was killed. And I said, Where? And he said, There he is, just below the shed by the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And how did you or your son know that he had been killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He saw him just below the shed when he was killed. From the hall. The window was open and the shed was beyond that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: You saw your husband lying over there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was lying there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And do you recall that he wore a uniform or other clothes, civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no. He was in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And you told about this Stojka coming in the house and grabbing a gun. Was that after you noticed your husband lying over there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Stojka came in -- she came in before. And then when she went out afterwards, Ibrahim -- I'm sorry. I'm having problems with my concentration. Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam, Madam, let me help you a little bit. If you need a rest, if you would like us to -- look at me. Look at me. If you would like us to stop for a little bit so that you can go in the room where you were before and rest for about 20 minutes or so, we can do that. I mean, the last thing we want to do is to see you suffering. Would you like to stop for the time being and we'll have a short break?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So with your indulgence we will have a 25-minute break now. And then the understanding is this: If necessary, we will stop again as we go along, not according to a tight schedule. Okay? All right? And I just would appeal for your cooperation, which I am sure I will find. Thank you. So we will have a 25-minute break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's proceed. Mr. Wubben, I've been thinking about the testimony of this witness during the break. I think we are having a lot of questions and a lot of answers about many facts that are not relevant. I mean, if we could restrict it to what you really need to prove by means of this witness, I think we will get it over and done with much earlier. Try to help the witness a little bit by directing her more specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because we don't need the entire story of what began -- what happened from the beginning to the end. We just need to know what is relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour. I will proceed accordingly. May I start?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Witness, let's take your statement from where you ended it before the break, and that was about this Ibrahim and Edem. What can you tell us about them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. When my husband was killed and Svetozar said, Mom, Dad was killed. And I said, Where was he killed? And he said, Just below the shed. Then Ibrahim ran into the house and my son told me to lie under the bed. And I said, they will catch us alive. He said, go lie under the bed. I actually kneeled next to the window. He was next to me. He took a hand grenade and through it into the kitchen when this other person was in the kitchen. The bomb exploded and he fell next to the table, next to the water faucet. After that we were in the house for a little bit longer and he told me, Mom, can you jump through the window after me? I said I can jump but I cannot escape. He said, You -- he touched Pero -- he was wearing Pero's coat and he felt in the pockets. There were keys, a watch, and a comb. He said, Mom, maybe you will see Pero before I do. So I took those things and put them in my pocket. I was wearing a blouse and a sweater and a skirt, all these clothes. But I wasn't wearing that much. And he gave me that. I put it in my pocket. And he said, I am going through the window and you go through the door and may God help us. He jumped and then I managed to take some poison before that, to drink it. He jolted it out of my hand and it fell in the hall. This was earlier. We didn't touch it. And then when he jumped through the window I grabbed poison, I poured it into a glass. Thank God there wasn't too much of it. I mixed it and drank it and I went outside of the door. Along the creek -- I knelt down in this creek. I was there on my knees and on my elbows and I was crawling through this creek, slowly, so that I would not break any branches. And my son, when he jumped through the window, all I could hear was that Nasir said, Hooray, give me a rope and a knife. And he jumped through the window. I later went out through the door and went to the woods. I was in the woods. There was a creek. There was a whole pile of branches. I crawled under these branches. I lay there. The water was underneath my right arm. It was after midnight. There was rain, there was thunder, lightning. There was water under me and there was water falling on top of me. And I was lying like that. And when the cocks began to crow in the morning, I went out and I was feeling my way slowly wherever there were branches on the ground. I was -- kept close to them. And I hid under a tree when it was -- there was lightning. I hid under this tree, this birch tree, and I was just trying to protect myself from the rain. And then I could see where I was supposed to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification. I have a question regarding this poison that you mentioned that you took. Why did you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but what is the relevance? I'm sorry, because this is the problem. What is the relevance of this?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: The relevance is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: She's still alive, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's proceed. We can't afford to waste time on matters that are not relevant for the case. It is obvious why people take poisons in difficult situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: When you ran outside the door, did you see any army, any men, any soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I didn't see any. I went out to the creek and went along the creek. Then I crawled under the branches and I was lying in this water underneath the branches. I didn't see any soldiers. I didn't see anyone. And I spent the night there. And then the next day when the cocks began to crow, I crawled out from under the branches and I went through the woods in semi-darkness. I was keeping close to the branches. And then when I came to -- under this birch tree it was raining and I was wiping the rain from my face. And then I looked and I wanted to see. I don't know, it looked maybe like a log or maybe somebody killed or I don't know. Anyway, I didn't dare go further. I returned to the creek and I crawled on my hands and knees along this creek. And when I got close to my house -- I didn't dare go to my house, but I was just going through the garden. I crossed through the garden and I went through the crossing to Milovan's garden. And I was near a plum tree and close to his house there was a sheet with two knots tied in this sheet. And I passed by there and left. This stayed behind. I came to Marko's house. Next to Marko's house --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please stop. Thank you for this clarification. I have a question. You went from the woods or from the creek towards houses. To what village or hamlet did you come first, when you saw this house or these houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was going to Radijevici. I was going towards Radijevici.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And where did you first come to Radijevici or first went through another hamlet or village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Divovici, which is where I lived, then Radijevici is next. So that's what I was going -- that's where I was going.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I have a question regarding this first village or hamlet called Divovici. What did you saw? Did you saw houses and what did you notice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me tell you, when I started going up from the creek and I crossed the garden through this crossing and in Milovan's garden, above the house I saw that thing tied in this sheet with two knots. And then I went above Milovan's house to Marko's house. Marko's house was broken, the door was open. I passed through the field above the house and I went across the creek and that's where my brother-in-law's house Stojan's was burning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Stop, please. Will you confirm to the Judges in which hamlet this was. What was the name of the hamlet or village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in Divovici, that one house burned down. Veljo's house, Stojan's house. The third house belonged to Milovan Djukic. Also Milos Djukic's auxiliary buildings, and Milos's barn. And Radovan's storage house. They all burned in Divovici. And then --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please, please. Wait for the question. What do you mean by burned down or burned? Were they damaged or were they smoking or did you saw fire? What can you tell the Judges about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All I could see was that things were destroyed. The walls were knocked down. The ground floor. And it looked as if the house had fallen down and the roof just collapsed on top of everything. And I just passed by there quickly and went to Radijevici. When I got close to Djukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Excuse me. Let me ask you a question before you get to Radijevici. In the hamlet you discussed or the village, what you saw, were all the houses destroyed or were all the houses damaged or partly damaged? Could you live there? If so, please clarify to the Judges.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, you could not live there. It was knocked down. You couldn't live in those houses that collapsed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And that was caused by burning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was burned. Those houses were burned. They were burning. There was no roof left, just the walls. All the houses had beams and lots of wood parts. There was no concrete like there is now, so that you could continue to live in a house like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now, you stated to the Judges earlier in your statement that there were 11 houses in your hamlet or village. Were all these houses damaged like that? Or not all of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's in Radijevici. There's one house, Stojan's house, and these other houses, one, two, three, four. Then up there, Milica's house, that's five; Radoje's house is six; Obren's house, seven; then Radivoje's house. There's more.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now, let's get --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All together with the barns and so on. I counted all of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes. But let's go back to Divovici -- please, Witness, please, Witness. Let's go back to Divovici. My question was: Were all the houses in that hamlet or village, how you name it, were they all damaged or partly? Can you please clarify to the Judges. All of them or just a few?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only two -- not all of them were damaged. Not all of them were damaged. People later returned. I forgot to say when I was there -- when I started to talk about that, when my Svetozar and I stayed in the house, when we were stuck in the house a bomb or something was thrown into my pantry. There was a little bit of concrete there because that was built on additionally. The window burned. The doors burned and also the box -- the wooden box where we stored the flour. Maybe there was a litre or two of brandy and some other things. It doesn't matter. All of that burned. The window and the door burned and also it caught a little bit on, further out. You couldn't stay in the house because of the smoke, but we didn't dare leave the house because of the enemy. I don't know what to call them. My son was doing like this in the house. He couldn't breathe because of the smoke and the sweat.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please. Please answer my questions and try to keep in mind what my question was. My question -- next question is: Who caused this damage of burning down, knocking down? Was it the enemy or was it someone else? Who caused this fire --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If the witness knows --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The enemy. The enemy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's obviously, but --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't see anyone else. The others were in the fields and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: What do you mean by the enemy? Serbians or another ethnic origin if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They couldn't be Serbs. They wouldn't burning and destroying, but it was the enemy. People who attacked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who were these people? Where did they come from? Who were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Muslims and those people. They were from the outside, from Orlici and I don't know, I forgot the places -- the name of the places. They attacked the Drina Valley. They were torching and killing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How do you know that they were Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My son told me that it was the Muslims. My son said, that's this Nasir [Realtime transcript read in error: "Naser"] Orlic who organised the army and is hitting the Drina Valley.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, objection to the transcript. The witness said Nasir Orlic. She said Nasir and not Naser.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know how to say it. Don't take it wrongly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Did you yourself recognise any of the attackers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't see anyone because I was in the house. I didn't see anyone. I cannot say that I saw someone if I did not. I was in the house. My son was there. I was in the room. He didn't let me go to the other rooms in the house because he was afraid that I would see something, that I would get frightened, that I would start moaning and crying. I can't say that I saw something if I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I take it that you are not in a position to tell us how many were these attackers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't see. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And did you at least see what they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I didn't. I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So you can't tell us whether they were wearing a uniform or whether they were wearing just civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I really couldn't tell you. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Witness, you told the Judges about this Ibrahim who entered your house. Can you tell them more about this Ibrahim. Is that a Muslim or a Serb?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Ibrahim, a Muslim. He is a Muslim from the neighbouring Zanjevo. It's close by. It's in the neighbourhood. He entered the house. He ran into the house and my Svetozar through this hand grenade and he fell there and he stayed behind in my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. My question is: This Ibrahim, was he armed or not? If you know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was armed. I don't know what his rifle was -- what kind it was, but he did have an ammunition on a belt around here. The belt had ammunition in it but I don't know what kind of a gun it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Do you recall if so that he wore a uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't really pay attention to that and I don't remember what kind of uniform it was. I don't even remember the rifle. All I know is that when I turned to go I could see this belt buckled around and the ammunition in this belt, but I don't know what kind of ammunition it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And, Witness, another name you called is the person who start yelling or calling something after your son jumped out of the kitchen window. You mentioned a name. Can you tell more?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nasir Mahmutovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And where does he come from, can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Zanjevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And what was he calling or yelling?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He said, Hooray, give me a rope and a knife.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And did you hear any shots at that time, any shooting when your son left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went up into the woods. I could hear firing and shooting, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Okay. But my next question will be related to this Nasir Mahmutovic. Is he a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now I go further in your story that you told the Judges about the damaging, the burning down, of your own village. But then, after that, you went to the village of Radijevici, as you told us prior. What did you notice in that village --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: -- of? Was it the same damage or burning down as in your village of Divovici, or don't you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The houses that I was talking about, I came to Radijevici then I was expecting to see somebody. It was morning but there was nobody around. I reached a door, pushed the handle. There was nobody inside. I went to another door of another person, it was closed. Then I came back again and passed by that person's field and house. And I stopped at a certain point in this field. There was nobody around. I came down to the road. I looked up and down the road. There was nobody there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. The question is: Did you notice any damaging or burning down? If so, is it the same as you saw in Divovici? Or as far as you know, there was no damage at all in Radijevici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't see or pay attention to that. There were just these houses that had burned down. I didn't really pay attention or see anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: But these houses that were burned down, did you notice specific houses of families and can you call the names of those families, if so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is Milovan's -- are you talking both about Divovici and Radijevici?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Or only Radijevici? There's Obren there, Milic Obren's house; the barn. Milica's house; and Obren's barn; and Radoje's house. They burned. And Radivoje's. But nothing other than that burned in Radijevici.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And did you notice when you passed through your own hamlet or village of Divovici and then to Radijevici, did you notice any military men or military equipment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't see anyone. I didn't see any alive or dead people when I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So also no Serbian soldiers or Serbian military equipment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't see anyone when I went down there, when I crossed the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Then, as you stated to the Judges, you went to a field. What happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then Zdravko asked me there, when I crossed the road, Zdravko said, Savka is coming. I went down into the fields and he said, Let me take you down to the Drina. And I went to the Drina. We approached the bank. And then I saw Milos, old Milos. And I told him, You should go back. I will go to Milos.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And did you notice what happened with your son or husband?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My son's eye was gouged out and one of his arms was broken. And my husband, in all that trouble of mine and all my tears, it seemed to me as if he was without a head, but I don't -- I'm not quite sure. I don't dare say that. Later when I recovered my composure, I don't know. I was grieving then, so I didn't really see it so well. But I did see my son clearly. I didn't see my husband so clearly. I was more dealing with my son than with my husband.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And did you notice other harm to your son on his body, specific part?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, under his neck there was a bruise.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And when did you find out about the fate of your husband and son? Was that the same day or later on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The next day. They left on Tuesday when they were picking up the dead, and on Wednesday I went to the burial in Bajina Basta.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And did you subsequently return to your house, to your farmhouse?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I know that I was in, Serbia across the Drina River, saying with a relative of mine. I stayed there until everything was done and over, and then my daughter-in-law came and took me to Obrenovac where my brother lived. I wasn't allowed to go anywhere else. On the fifth or the sixth day when I went there was firing from the hill and we ran. And I never went there again.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Was that the fifth or the sixth day after the attack, do you mean that, or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was more. I called some people. I brought two couches, sofas, and that was the only thing I brought to Serbia because I know there was no one there to buy anything for me and supplies or anything. So I carried that with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: May I stop you here. My question is: When did you actually return to your house, to your farm? To go in --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We returned the next spring when we had to sow for the crops, the corn and the vegetables.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And what did you see when you got into your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was soot. There had been a fire in the house. The house was full of soot and dust. My neighbour and myself, we brought some kitchenware and some rags and we washed those and rinsed those and she tried to wash the soot away. The house, the hall, everything was washed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: My question is: Your house was damaged or not? Can you confirm.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The pantry damaged. Still, even now. Black, burned out. And the house was all -- the sides of the house were hit by bullets.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And the shed and barn, were they damaged or not, if so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The barn when I was in the woods up there, something just came down with a thud. I didn't know what it was. But when I came back and when they were gathering the dead bodies, my son was under a collapsed storage house and everything was lying on top of him, the slabs, and the pieces of wood and the wooden beams of the storage and everything. Only his legs were sticking out slightly from underneath all the rubble. They tied a rope around him because they were afraid that his body has been mined and they pulled his body out of the rubble, the rubble that was on top of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Witness, my next question is: Did you notice our -- the animals you referred to in the beginning of your statement? What happened with the animals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Gone. Chickens, maybe the fox had taken them away, carried them off, the swine also. The pig.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Sorry. And the goat and the cow?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The goat and the cow, my son had seen those. He said that Mahmutovic had taken them away and he threw the door into the barn.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Who is that person? Was that during the attack? And who is that person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During the attack, that's when it was. He's a neighbour of ours from Zanjevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Is he a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: My last questions will be related to the damage to your house and some information of your husband and son. Let's start with the last issue. So in your opinion, your son and -- pardon. Stop, please. Please listen to the question. Is it in your opinion, can you confirm to the Judges, that your son and husband were village guards and not part of the army, if so --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Opinion evidence is for experts. She can merely state what she knows. Does she know whether they were village guards. I don't see that it's a matter of opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Basically we are still back to square one. I don't think we are going to get much from the witness in any case. In what capacity -- how come that your husband and your son found themselves defending the village? How were -- who armed them? Who gave them arms? And why were they --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And why were they given arms, weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know that. I never asked. They never told me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But there was a village guard, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Around the houses, yes, our houses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And your husband and your son formed part of that village guard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did they also form part of the army of Republika Srpska? Were they enrolled as conscripts of Republika Srpska, as soldiers of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Last question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Take your time. I'm not stopping you. The thing is if you give her a rope, she will run away with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I projected two issues, and last and second issue is:

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Did any organisation or person pay you for your damage, for the damage of your farm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Compensation. In other words, compensation. Did you receive compensation for the damage that you sustained on your house and your farm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you ask for compensation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We asked but we got none.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: That's it. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you know if anyone else in your village got compensation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Hold on. I did get something for the house, for the repairs. If that is what you refer to as "compensation," I did obtain that, yes. I got that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: But not for the animals --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I got money for the concrete. And for the pains, for example, I got nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And who did you receive that compensation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't get money. I got compensation in kind. They brought wooden beams and roof tiles and some paint. That's what I received but nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Wubben. Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, Madam, if you look the other side you are going to be asked a series of questions by Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Ms. Djokic, to assist you to give short answers, if you see my hand making this gesture, if you would stop there, if you follow me. Now, firstly today you mentioned some of the Muslims who you saw on the 5th of October and you mentioned Ibrahim who your son killed with a handgun.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't see. I didn't see -- yes, Ibrahim, yes. He was in the house, my son killed. We had to defend ourselves when the attack occurred and he attacked us in the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'll come back to that but that's Ibrahim Mujkic from Zanjevo, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not Mujkic, Ibrahim --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: His surname is not important.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What's his last name, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If you can't remember, don't worry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. We will clear it because even in her two statements she never remembered the name of that person. Did he have a nickname? Did he have a nickname, this Ibrahim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it was Kokica, Ibrahim Kokica. And I don't know his last name. I never knew his last name, in fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. That's enough. Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And Nasir Mahmutovic, someone whose voice you heard on the day, on the 5th of October; that's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did hear it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And before the war you used to hire him to cut wood and to transport fertiliser for your field because he had a tractor and a chain saw, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And Edem Mahmutovic, who is a person you said maybe your son saw took your cow and goat away, he's also from Zanjevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So it's right, isn't it, that all of the Muslims you heard and saw on that day, the 5th of October, were Zanjevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't see all of them. I didn't see all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Also said earlier -- my apologies, I'll slow down. And I'm referring to page 29, line 10 of the transcript, just for everyone else's benefit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Page 29.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Line 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: When asked as to who the attackers were, part of your response was: "They were from the outside, from Orlici." And then you went on. Now, what I want to ask you is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Were in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you know the area of Zapolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't. I hardly ever leave home. I'm illiterate. I don't really leave home.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you know a village called Gornja Olica in that region?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So as to Orlici, that's not a place which you're familiar with? If you could answer, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to go back to the Zanjevo Muslims. It's right, isn't it, that the Muslims from Zanjevo had to leave their homes in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They went away without rifles with no gunfire whatsoever. But then later, they killed us like dogs and when they left they were perfectly healthy and whole. Why they left, I don't know. That's what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Ms. Djokic, I'll ask you not to add your own commentary, if you don't mind. Just answer the questions put to you. Now, I'm going to ask you about a couple of incidents near the beginning of the war and ask you if you recall them. The first one, and tell me just if you recall this, in the middle of May 1992 you were in Radijevici and you saw Nura Osmanovic from Zanjevo. And she was crying because she had to leave Zanjevo and she had to leave cattle with Vitomir Stjepanovic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Who did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Nura Osmanovic. Do you recall that she had to leave her cattle with Vitomir Stjepanovic because she had to leave her home and farm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, she didn't leave it to Vitomir.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Who did she leave it with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No one. In Divovici, with no one. I don't know that she left it with anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So that incident is not something that you recall, Nura Osmanovic leaving her cattle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, second incident later, perhaps in September 1992 -- sorry, you were going to say something.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Perhaps later in the year, isn't it right that the village guards from your village saw Nasir and Fejzo Mahmutovic passing above your village but the village guards left them alone because they thought they had gone to take food from their homes? Do you recall that incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No. This is something I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Were you aware around this time, September 1992, that the Muslims from Zanjevo were suffering from severe food shortages because they had to leave their cattle and crops behind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. We had shortages, too. I don't know about their crops, what happened with their crops. I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, just coming to the village guard. I think you've agreed today that there was an armed village guard in Divovici. It's right, isn't it, that your husband was in the guard and your son as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were in their houses, but they didn't go anywhere further than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's right, isn't it, that your husband, Sreten, had a rifle? You can answer the question straightforwardly. It's a straightforward question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he didn't, not on that day. We were working. We were chopping wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm not asking whether on that day he had a rifle. I'm asking whether your husband in 1992 possessed a rifle. Are you reluctant to answer the question, Mrs. Djokic? It's a simple question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did he have a weapon, your husband?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, he did. But he didn't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What weapon did he have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Was it -- now, let's say a year before all this happened, did he have a weapon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I don't know when, for example, this was or anything. He didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Was your husband a hunter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So do I take it that you did not have a shotgun, your husband did not have a hunting shotgun?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know about these different types of rifles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But before these incidents, before we come to these incidents in October of 1992, do you remember seeing a weapon in your house belonging to your husband or to your son?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In our house? Well, there was my son's weapon in the house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And do you remember -- do you recall when your son brought the weapon into the house the first time? How --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How far --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- then when this was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But was it a few days before the 5th of October? Was it weeks? Was it months? Was it years?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Seven days. Seven days earlier, that's when I saw the weapon. But not before then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And seven days, more or less. Seven days before the 5th of October when you saw your son's weapon. Did you also notice that your husband, too, had a weapon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My husband had a weapon but I don't know what kind. But --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm obliged, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think I got there a little bit in an indirect manner, but I suggest you carry on from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Or if you want to proceed to something different, it's up to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I've got a few more questions on a similar theme anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your son also, as you discovered on the 5th of October, 1992, had grenades as well, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Grenade, yeah. It was thrown -- he threw it after to defend himself from Ibrahim when Ibrahim came storming into our house.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We'll come to that. But it's right, isn't it, that your son had a bomb or a grenade or however you want to describe it which he used on the 5th of October to kill another person? So he had grenades, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had -- I'm not sure whether he had any more grenades with the exception of the one that he actually threw.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And Pero, your son-in-law, also had a rifle, didn't he? You've told us today.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not my son-in-law. He's my nephew, not my son-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, he had a rifle, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Is there any reason, Mrs. Djokic, why you're so reluctant to admit that these men had weapons? Because you seem not to be very happy about answering these questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, objection sustained. Objection sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm curious --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now come on, Mr. Jones, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, if those men all had rifles, isn't it right that also all the men in the village had weapons in Divovici.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How am I supposed to know about all of them? I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you know who gave your son the grenade or bomb that he used on the 5th of October?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have no idea. Nor did I ask, nor did he ever tell me anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Let's move on to the attack of the 5th of October. It's right, isn't it, that you were in your home when the attack started and your heard shooting. And so you don't know, do you, who started the shooting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And your son gave you a gun. And it is a big gun, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The gun your son gave you was a large weapon, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know what sort of a weapon it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Isn't it right that the clip which was put into the gun was the size of your hand more or less? That's how I believe you've described it in earlier statements.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was like this, the clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And was it a clip which went into the bottom or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know what sort it was. I'm telling you, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's fine. But this was an ammunition clip, wasn't it? It wasn't an individual bullet which you were putting into the gun?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Only answer if you know. Was it a machine-gun that your son gave you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And your son's idea when he gave you that gun was that you would shoot from the house at the Muslims who had come into your village in order to kill them if need be, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, one had to defend oneself so that they would not catch him alive. But still, they got to him and tortured him.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: At that point when he gave you the gun, it's right, isn't it, that no one had shot at you or threatened your life?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Shooting, yes. When the walls were all pockmarked by bullets from all sides, from above, from below. They were firing from everywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But no one had shot directly at you at that point or at your son.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were inside the house and they were shooting outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your neighbour --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And through the windows.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your neighbour Stojka Stjepanovic came around and said, Come out, the people won't hurt you. These are our neighbours. They will do you no harm. Didn't she?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. She came to the house and she yelled, Come on, Savka, come out of the house. All of these people are our neighbours. They won't do us any harm, they said so. But we didn't have the courage to go out.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Instead, you told us today, we defended ourselves from the house, which I take it to mean, and correct me if I'm wrong, that you were shooting at the Muslims who had come into your village.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You also were shooting, at least your son was shooting, wasn't he, from the window of the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, from the door up there and around the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Did you see if your son killed anyone when he was shooting from the window?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't, except for Ibrahim, but that was inside the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And isn't -- is it right that your neighbours were also -- your Serb neighbours were also shooting because Stojka was going to their houses as well and imploring them to come out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't see that. I only saw her come to my house. But I didn't see her go anywhere else because I was not able to see anything else from my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So just to be clear, it's right, isn't it, that you and your son on that day, the 5th of October, were getting ready to fight to the death essentially, even though your neighbours from Zanjevo had been friends before the war and had not hurt you up to that point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Up to that point, no, never. I couldn't say that we had quarrel. We would be passing across each other's fields. Nobody barred anybody else from doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So why is it on the 5th of October you were so afraid of your former neighbours that you felt that you had to take this desperate action? Was it from what you had heard on TV and radio or rumours or something of that nature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because of the voices. There was shouting around the house. They were saying, Come out, you Chetniks. And that's what we heard around. So we didn't dare go outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Were you in any doubt, though, when you and your son picked up weapons and started shooting at these Muslims from your home that they would treat you like soldiers and shoot back at you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. We were afraid of that and we didn't dare come out of the house and trust them that they would not harm us.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Stojka --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Objection to the question itself. I take it that my learned friend doesn't mean with his question, when I look at the transcript that she, the witness herself, also started shooting. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I can clarify --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, it --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not, I did not. And I don't know how.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It is correct. You are right, Mr. Wubben. Because the suggestion was that both her husband -- her son and herself picked up weapons and started shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: My apologies. If I may clarify that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not. I did not pick up any weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think we can leave it and proceed. It's obvious now. Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, when Stojka came into your house later and tried to take your son's gun off him, he told her to let go or he would kill her, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And then after Stojka left, Ibrahim came in and --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Ibrahim came in. He told me, Mom, lie down next to the couch. And I went down on my knees and elbows. And then he was above my head --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If you could just answer the questions which I ask. Ibrahim came in also to persuade you to leave your house, didn't he? That was his purpose of coming in.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he didn't say anything. As he came in, my son threw the bomb. He didn't come in with empty hands. He was carrying a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But it's right, isn't it, Ibrahim came into your kitchen, didn't say anything threatening or shoot at you, and your son threw in a grenade and killed him. That's the basic fact, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. You stopped her when she was trying to explain what happened when Ibrahim walked into the house and went along with that, but not anticipating that you were then going to suggest what you are suggesting now. Now, Madam, look at me. Tell me exactly how it happened. Ibrahim walks or storms into your house. He asks you to do what? What did he ask you to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He stormed in and this other one, my son, threw the hand grenade and he was left lying there. We didn't dare wait for anything with both of us in the house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But when he stormed into the house, did he tell you to kneel down or to do something? You started telling us that he told you to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, he didn't tell me, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ibrahim didn't tell you to lie down near the carpet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, he didn't say anything. As soon as he stormed in, this other one, my son, threw the grenade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: He walked in and got killed, basically?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Objection. She first said it was not walking in, it was more running in or something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stormed in, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So when my learned friend takes that as walking in, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He didn't knock at the door and say, Madam Djokic, can I come? He just stormed in.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He stormed into the house and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Let's move forward to another thing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think so, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And I'm going to ask you first about some of the property which you lost that day. You've mentioned a cow and a goat and they were stolen from Edem Mahmutovic from Zanjevo, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And as for the rest of your livestock, you don't know whether they wandered off on their own, whether they were eaten by foxes --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
