utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know. I went to Serbia later. I went to Obrenovac and all of that was left behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, to go back to your house and the damage to that house, is it right that there was actually a fire started on that day, the 5th of October, or was it subsequently? I wasn't clear from your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. On the 5th of October when we were in the house it was thrown in and it exploded, and then it started to smoke and there was -- there were flames. And we were in the house, so we couldn't stay in the house because of the smoke and we couldn't go outside because of the enemy.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And that fire was possibly started by Stojka Stjepanovic, wasn't it, because shortly before you heard her discussing or being told to set your house on fire.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not Stojka.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You don't know who set your house on fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know who set it on fire because Stojka could not do it. There's a large -- there was a large hole in the house when this thing exploded. It had to have been something thrown in by somebody from the woods, and it came in through the window and it made a big hole in the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: How far are the woods from your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not that far. Maybe about 10, 15 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So you're saying you think it's a person who could have thrown this bomb or a weapon? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know who it was. I can't say who it was when I don't know. I know that it was thrown in. There's a hole. The hole is still there next to the -- next to the pantry. The whole house is --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, thanks. Mrs. Djokic, if you could keep your answers short, please. If there's a pause it's because we're waiting for the interpretation, not necessarily because we want you to go on. Now, would you accept the following suggestion which I'm going to make to you that the Muslims outside your house were being shot at by your son and they wanted to smoke you out of your house so that you would stop shooting at them, and that is why your house was set on fire? Would you accept that suggestion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As if my son was shooting? He wasn't shooting except for when Ibrahim stormed in, then he threw the hand grenade. He did hold a rifle. He was firing -- he was firing up there and defending himself. He was defending himself. He had to defend himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: What I'm saying to you, Mrs. Djokic, is your son at least posed a danger to the people outside. And my suggestion was that the reason why a bomb or whatever was thrown into your house was to stop you posing a danger to those people outside. My question is: Do you accept that that is in fact what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He could not pose a danger to them. He was only firing from the door or perhaps if he went to the window. He couldn't really fire at anyone if one of them was behind one side of the house or on the other side behind the house. He couldn't do anything. He was shooting maybe up in the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's right, isn't it, that only your cold room or pantry was burned. Your whole house wasn't destroyed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not the whole house.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And staying with Divovici, it's right, isn't it, that the barn of Vidoje Djukic was damaged but not his house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The barn, the barn was damaged of Vidoje Djukic and not the -- I don't know about the grain storage. I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But not the -- sorry. I think there might be a difficulty with the translation. I can repeat the translation but I think it was clear. The house of Vidoje Djukic was not damaged, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Nor the house of Milos Djukic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The auxiliary building of Milos was destroyed and the stable of Milos Djukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But not his main house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Milos's main house was preserved. The outbuilding was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: In fact, it's right, isn't it, that in Divovici only two or three houses and a couple of barns suffered fire damage out of 11 houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were barns and houses and I've already said which ones had burned. I didn't say that all the houses were burned, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But the majority of houses were not burned. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was one, two -- one, two, three, and the outbuilding, four. This was in Divovici. Four houses were burned. And then two barns burned down. That's for Divovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. And for the houses which weren't damaged, it was perfectly possible for people to live in those houses after the 5th of October.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, to live.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, coming to Radijevici, there it's right, isn't it, that it's a question of essentially four buildings, the barn of Obren Vasic but not his house; the house of Radoje Bozic, but not his barn; and the house of Radivoje Katanic, but not his barn; and the house of Milic, but not his barn. Is that a correct summary?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Minic's. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's out of 25 houses in Radijevici.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The total houses in Radijevici, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know how many there are houses there in total. I just thought you said that all those houses had burned down and that's not so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned you lost your son that day and that you learned that he was missing an eye. It's right, isn't it, that that could have happened after he had been killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, broken. I don't know if it was when he was killed or when he was tortured. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Didn't you tell us today that he was actually found under a collapsed building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, underneath the storage house. We call it a storage house, but it's not a building.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, just a couple more questions. You've also told us today that your son told you at the beginning of the attack that he knew which forces were attacking you. That's what you've told us today. Now, it's right, isn't it, that you made a statement in 1994, firstly. Do you recall making a statement in 1994?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I know the year.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And it's right, isn't it -- let me rephrase that. First --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are not aware of this statement. We don't even have a copy of it. At least I don't. I have got a statement which goes back to the 25th of March of the year 2000. And then another statement which goes back to the 20th of October of the year 2003.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, we have a spare copy which we'll pass up. I apologise if Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. It's not your fault, in any case.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: When you made that statement, Mrs. Djokic, you were aware, weren't you, that it was for the purposes of a criminal investigation?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Would you repeat your answer, please, Mrs. Djokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The interpreters couldn't hear you, Madam. Could you repeat the answer, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I'm just listening.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'll ask another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: When you were asked about these events in 1994, you were aware, weren't you, that this was an important matter, an investigation, that it was important that you tell the truth, the whole truth, about everything that you knew about the attack on your village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told them what I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And this was a year or so after the attack on your village, wasn't it, the first statement you gave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know when we went to give this statement. I can't know that. I'm illiterate. I didn't ask for the dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The date -- the precise date isn't important. It was within a reasonable time, within a year or so, of these events happening, wasn't it, that you first spoke about the attack on your village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was on the 5th of October, the attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's right, isn't it, that in the first statement you gave about these events, you nowhere mentioned that your son said anything to you about who might be attacking your village. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe I forgot or I didn't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: This is a statement which I'm talking about which you made not now, 12 years after the events, but a year or two within the events. Are you saying you forgot then, but you've remembered again the conversation since?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember that when this man --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Which man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't then when I was giving the statement, but now I -- I'm -- it's about this man who was attacking.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. So sorry, I'm still not following you. Did you when you gave your first statement, are you saying you had forgotten about a conversation which you had with your son and you've now remembered it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: She's just saying that she acknowledges that she may not have mentioned it during -- in the course of this statement but she is remembering now. So.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's right, isn't it, that you subsequently made two more statements, this time to the Prosecutor or investigators of this Tribunal. Do you remember that, making statements to the Office of the Prosecutor or investigators of the International Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's right, isn't it, that in neither of those statements either, though you mention a great deal of the events you've told us about today, again there's no mention of your son telling you anything about who might be attacking your village. Isn't that right? Can you please speak up.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I forgot.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: This would have been a very important thing to mention, Mrs. Djokic, wouldn't it? These are among the last words that your son ever said to you. Are you really saying that you forgot for 12 years that he said these things to you, and now 12 years later in The Hague you've all of a sudden remembered? Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He told me that then, but I didn't mention it. It didn't occur to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: This is about the people who attacked your village. Surely all this time you would have realised that if this conversation did take place that that was a very important matter that you would have had to mention to people who asked you about these events and you would have mentioned it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It follows, Your Honour, this is a very important point for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but I suggest -- you've had your answer about six times already. This is the position. She is not offering you an explanation. She is just telling you, then I didn't say it; now I am remembering it and I am saying it. Let the Chamber draw its own conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: May I make one last suggestion to the witness or question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Has someone suggested to you, Mrs. Djokic, that you should mention now a conversation which you had never mentioned before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, nobody told me anything. Nobody told me anything. No one told me anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I suggest that we are almost supposedly nearing the time for the break, but instead of -- shall we conclude now --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but it's easy for you to say it's okay, Mr. Wubben. What I want to know is whether the rest of the staff behind the glass -- I don't think we have more than a few minutes. How many -- how much time do you require?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I have a couple of questions. I would need limited to five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One, two -- so can we overstay by about 10 minutes, 15 minutes, and then it will be over? Okay. I see from behind the glass okay. So let's proceed. We are soon going to finish, Madam Djokic. So bear with us a little bit more and then it will be over and you can go back home. Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: When you were in the house during the attack, you told the Judges that your son was shooting. What was he aiming at precisely and why was he shooting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How can I know? He was firing so that nobody would enter the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And was he the only person --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So that nobody would run into the house. Perhaps that's why he was shooting. He was afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: He was afraid. And you were afraid as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And was your son the only person who was shooting at the time or at the same time there were more shooting from other persons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was shooting from up there, from the sides. And he was afraid that somebody wouldn't run into the house and kill us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And at that very time of this shooting of this Ibrahim storming in, did you notice that your village was under attack or did you pay only attention to your own house if so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was completely attacked, all of it, on the 5th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: What do you mean by that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was attacked Boljevici, Radijevici, Kutijesi. This is something I heard later when I crossed the Drina, that there were attacks. There were houses which burned in Boljevici as well, but I don't know much about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Next question. And may I take it when your son was shooting and acting like this in your house, was he defending you and himself in your house?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's an extremely loaded question, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In our house he was defending us.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's an opinion of who's defending and who's attacking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go, go. She understood what was happening --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: She understood what was happening, that her son was defending himself -- herself and also the house. That's her opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: May I ask you: Who in fact did kill your husband?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know. I don't know who killed who. But when my husband was killed, that was when Ibrahim came barging into our house and that was when my son threw the grenade.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And did your son throw the grenade to defend himself also or was there another reason? Why should he throw a grenade to someone storming in his house?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: He asking her to speculate about the motives of his son.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't even think there is room for speculation. It's obvious to me. I don't need the witness to explain this. There was an attack and all of a sudden you have someone storm in the house with a rifle and ammunition round has --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This Ibrahim, he came in carrying a rifle, but no one else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: You were referring to a name. Correct me --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, if re-examination is to be confined to matters raised in cross-examination. I didn't raise issues of names --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But I haven't heard the question as of yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But I'm anticipating --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let us see. I will stop him if he goes beyond. I don't know what the question is.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's only I deliberately avoided getting into the whole question of names and there were questions which I would have asked otherwise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You put the surname of Mujkic or Mujkic to the witness and she have never mentioned it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I recall a list of names of -- house --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead, Mr. Wubben, but you know what the limitations of re-examination are -- should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: In your answering of the question of the counsel of the other side, you referred to a name, and correct me if I'm wrong, Orlici. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, she had mentioned Orlici in her testimony and he --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Orlic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- and Mr. Jones referred her to that. So go straight. In other words, she had mentioned Orlici.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: What did you mean by a name called Orlici? Did you mean a place or a region or a person? What did you mean by it or something else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I meant a person probably who was attacking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Wait a moment. Quite a few minutes ago, Madam, you were asked the question: "When asked as to who the attackers were," part of your response was: "They were from outside, from Orlici." Actually, earlier on --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Orlic, Orlic, like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Earlier on I myself had asked you: Who were these people? Where did they come from? Where were they? And according to the transcript -- one moment. Let me finish. I am just trying to help you to explain. And when I asked you this question almost more than an hour ago, you told me: Muslims and those people. They were from outside, from Orlici. And I don't know. I forgot the places, the name of the places. They attacked the Drina Valley. They were torching and killing. So when you mentioned "Orlici," were you referring to a place or were you referring to a person? Because the way I read it here you are referring to a place.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a person, not a place. A person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you know of any place called Orlici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Does that name "Orlici" refer to a person called Naser Oric or --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Excuse me, that's outrageous.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Don't answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's an outrageous question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I withdraw this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Does that -- let me rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I think my learned friend should move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I will stop the witness from answering if it's not -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: If you don't know a name like that referring to a place, does that name that you called Orlici refer to a specific name of a person or not, or don't you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The person that led the army. That was Nasir Orlic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. That's finalised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Judge Brydensholt. Judge Brydensholt, to my right, would like to put a question to you, Madam, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: You mentioned that your neighbour I think it was, Stojka, came into your house twice actually and asked you to go out and asked your son to leave his gun behind. What -- do you know what happened in other houses --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, she grabbed the rifle. She grabbed the rifle when she came over to call us to come out and she grabbed the rifle that Svetozar was holding and she said, come out, Svetozar, our neighbours are out there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Do you know if she went to other houses and asked the other villagers to go out --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know. I didn't see anything. I didn't hear anything. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Later on have you heard that any of the inhabitants went out? What happened to the other inhabitants, the other neighbours you had in the hamlet? What happened to them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They all ran away. They all escaped. They were picking corn out in the field, and whoever heard the sounds of shooting, those people just tried to escape. There was no one left in the houses with the exception of Sujika. Sujika was the only one left and her grandchildren stayed back in Milovan's house. They were alive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to Stojka herself?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't get the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you repeat -- can I ask you to repeat your answer, please, because the interpreters couldn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] She was killed near the storage facility down there. That's at least what I heard. They found her. My Svetozar was there, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Judge Eser would like to put some questions to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I only want to ask you one question. You told us that not all houses have been burned but that barns have been burned down. Now, my question is: These barns, have they been empty or have there been some crops before or later on? What was the situation of these barns?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, the barns didn't burn down. They collapsed. They were knocked down. That was my storage facility that was knocked down and it fell down on top of my son. As for the other storage facilities in Divovici, those were not burned down, just the houses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. I have a final question for you, Madam. On that day when you lost your husband and also your son, do you remember seeing a certain Aris Ridic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that, but I am not sure and I never mentioned it again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you remember seeing Izet Hasanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Izet, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Izet Hasanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: My last question: Vidoje Djukic and Radovan Djukic, was there any shooting that you may know of from their house? Were they offering resistance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't see that. I didn't see that. I only heard sounds of moaning from their house but I don't know who was moaning. It was during the attack.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And that's the end of it, Madam Djokic. We have finished with your testimony. You are free to go back home now. You will soon be escorted out of this courtroom by Madam Usher, but before you leave this courtroom on my own behalf, on behalf of Judge Brydensholt and on behalf of Judge Eser and also on behalf of the Tribunal, I would like to thank you for having come over to give testimony, to give evidence in this trial. I can assure you that once you're out of this courtroom you will be attended to and you will receive all the assistance you require to enable you to return back home. Our last words on behalf of everyone, I wish you a safe journey back home. Thank you. Wait, wait, wait, wait. We go into private session, please, because she will be leaving her place and going out. So that no one can see your face.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And that again I must show you both my appreciation for having conducted the direct and the cross in really good time. Tomorrow we have the next witness. I won't mention the name, I'll just refer him as number 5 on the list that I have available. Right. I take it that you still require two hours, more or less?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: More or less, Your Honour. You -- well, as a lawyer you can say after proofing more, but we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, no. More or less. I want to make sure we can finish with this witness tomorrow. And Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will do my best as usual, but we shall take at least two hours no cross-examine this particular witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. That's fine. I think we can adjourn for today. I wish to thank also the rest of the staff as usual, the very cooperative interpreters and technical staff. And I wish that to make a public statement on this, I usually do. This has been going on for quite a few days. We have managed to finish the testimony of practically one witness per day, and that's thanks to you but also thanks to the cooperation of the interpreters and the technical staff that had stayed with us overtime, sort of. And I wish that this part of the record of today be transmitted to the heads -- the respective -- the heads of the respective units, translation, technical, et cetera, and also to the President of this Tribunal, because I think he ought to know that the cooperation of the staff, apart from counsel on both sides, is contributing to a large extent to reducing the time frame that we are taking to conclude our cases. I thank you all. We will meet again tomorrow morning at 9.00. I'm not quite sure but I think it's still in this courtroom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 29th day of October, 2004, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 12.15 p.m.,
